Question: How early do I have to be parked for a passenger who is landing?
Expected response: 15 minutes before their flight lands, by its latest estimate, or 30 minutes before for a Governing Body (GBA) passenger. Parked means in the parking lot. Nothing is subtracted for getting off the plane: the deplane allowance is a maximum, and a passenger with only a carry-on can be at the curb in ten minutes.

Question: When can I leave the airport after picking someone up?
Expected response: 45 minutes after their flight lands for a domestic flight (bags). For an international flight, 105 minutes: 45 for bags plus 60 for customs. With several flights at one stop, the one that lands last decides when you may leave.

Question: I have two passengers on different flights at the same stop. Which flight do I plan around?
Expected response: Both, for different things. The flight that lands first sets when you must be parked; the one that lands last sets when you may leave. Be there for the earliest, leave after the latest. If the first one is delayed past the second, they swap jobs.

Question: When does a drop-off for a departing flight have to happen?
Expected response: By the passenger's check-in deadline: 2 hours before departure for a domestic flight, 3 hours for an international one, counted from the earlier of the scheduled and the estimated departure. That is the time to be parked at the terminal.

Question: My departing passenger's flight is delayed 40 minutes. Should I pick them up later?
Expected response: No. A delay does not move the check-in desk: the deadline still counts from the scheduled departure, so you leave as dispatch planned.

Question: What if you can't tell whether a flight is international?
Expected response: Then the longer allowance is used: 3 hours for check-in and 105 minutes after landing. Guessing domestic could leave you late; guessing international only means waiting.

Question: My flight is running late. Will you change the time dispatch gave me?
Expected response: No. Dispatch's time stays as dispatch printed it. The delay is reported beside it, named for the flight that caused it, with the new parked-by and leaving times as the app's own numbers. The plan stays dispatch's.

Question: Can you put my stops in a faster order?
Expected response: No. Curbside converts dispatch's sheet; it does not plan the run, re-order it or suggest a different one. The stops stay in dispatch's order. You may change anything you need to yourself, and the change is marked as yours with dispatch's original kept beside it.

Question: Can I change the time of one of my stops?
Expected response: Yes. Your time is kept as yours, beside dispatch's, and the clocks and alerts run on yours from then on. Dispatch's original stays visible, and your change never re-orders dispatch's stops.

Question: The sheet names an airline Curbside doesn't know. What is the flight number?
Expected response: Curbside does not guess it: a wrong airline code makes a real-looking flight number for the wrong flight. The row says the airline could not be read. You can fix the flight yourself, and teach Curbside the airline's code so later sheets fill it in, marked as learned.

Question: How often are my flights checked?
Expected response: An arriving flight is checked about 3 hours before it lands, about 45 minutes before, and about 15 minutes after. A departing flight is checked once, about 3 hours before take-off: a later departure never moves the drop-off. A check is skipped when the next one is less than 40 minutes away.

Question: Why didn't I get an alert when my flight moved by 3 minutes?
Expected response: A change under 5 minutes is noise: estimates move by a minute or two all evening. Alerts go out when one of your times moves by 5 minutes or more, or when a flight lands, is cancelled or diverted, or changes terminal or belt.

Question: Which alerts are urgent?
Expected response: A flight landing early, or early enough that you must leave sooner, is urgent: it takes time away from you. A cancellation or diversion is urgent and says to call dispatch. A delay is calm, because it gives you time. Governing Body runs are one level louder.

Question: Dispatch sent the same run twice. Which copy counts?
Expected response: The one printed last, by the print time in the sheet's footer, whatever order they arrived in. The same assignment number updates the run in place.

Question: Do my corrections survive when dispatch re-sends the sheet?
Expected response: Yes. Corrections are kept apart from dispatch's sheet and applied again to every new copy. Where the new sheet disagrees with what you saw when you made the change, both are shown and you choose: keep mine, or use the sheet. A correction that can no longer be placed is kept and shown, never put on a different row.

Question: A passenger didn't show up. What do I do in Curbside?
Expected response: Mark them not coming. That takes them off all their rows on this run, pickup and drop-off, with one undo that never expires. Nothing is deleted: dispatch's row stays, shown as not coming, and their flight stops setting your clocks.

Question: Send my message to the passengers.
Expected response: Curbside never sends a message. It fills in your message for that kind of trip and opens it in WhatsApp, or in Messages when there is no WhatsApp, and you send it yourself.

Question: How long are my runs kept?
Expected response: A finished run leaves the main list 10 hours after it ends and stays in the archive. It is deleted 7 days after it ends, or after 2, 14 or 30 days if that is the setting chosen.

Question: What is a GB run?
Expected response: A Governing Body run: a row tagged GBA (arriving) or GBD (departing). A GB arrival gets 30 minutes before landing instead of 15, its alerts are one level louder and carry GOVERNING BODY, and a GB row is never combined with other requests without the on-site overseer.

Question: The sheet has a train (TD) or embassy (HO) row. What happens to it?
Expected response: Those rows are not supported yet. They are kept and shown as not supported, and listed as something the reader could not do, never left out silently and never guessed.

Question: Can I import a photo or screenshot of the sheet?
Expected response: No, only dispatch's PDF. A picture is pixels, not text, and misread digits would give wrong times and flight numbers. A PDF with no text in it is refused as a picture.
